profiles.name: Mangal Pandey
profiles.bio: A sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry whose action at Barrackpore preceded the wider 1857 uprising.
profiles.role: On 29 March 1857 he attacked British officers at Barrackpore. He was tried and executed on 8 April 1857.
profiles.context: His episode became a symbol of the uprising, whose causes also included annexation, service grievances, land policies and religious-cultural anxieties.

profiles.name: Rani Lakshmibai
profiles.bio: The queen of Jhansi who became a prominent military leader during the 1857 uprising.
profiles.role: She resisted British annexation of Jhansi and led forces during the uprising; she died fighting near Gwalior in June 1858.
profiles.context: Her role is often remembered as a symbol of resistance, though accounts of her campaigns vary.

profiles.name: Begum Hazrat Mahal
profiles.bio: A leader of resistance in Awadh during the 1857 uprising.
profiles.role: She helped organise opposition to Company authority in Lucknow and supported the proclamation of her son, Birjis Qadr, as ruler.
profiles.context: Her leadership highlights the participation of women and regional courts in the 1857 uprising.

profiles.name: Kunwar Singh
profiles.bio: A zamindar of Jagdishpur who led armed resistance in Bihar during the 1857 uprising.
profiles.role: At an advanced age, he led campaigns against Company forces and briefly recovered Jagdishpur.
profiles.context: His role is central to the regional history of the uprising in Bihar.

profiles.name: Tantia Tope
profiles.bio: A military leader who played a major role in the 1857 uprising after the rebellion spread from north India.
profiles.role: He campaigned with forces associated with Nana Sahib and Rani Lakshmibai and continued resistance through mobile warfare.
profiles.context: Captured after the uprising, he was tried and executed in 1859.

profiles.name: Vasudev Balwant Phadke
profiles.bio: An early anti-colonial organiser who built a small armed group in western India.
profiles.role: He sought to challenge colonial rule and mobilised support among sections of rural society in the 1870s.
profiles.context: His movement is often discussed as an early precursor to later revolutionary organisations.

profiles.name: Shyamji Krishna Varma
profiles.bio: A political activist who established India House in London and supported anti-colonial writing and organising.
profiles.role: He founded The Indian Sociologist and helped provide a meeting place for Indian students and activists in Britain.
profiles.context: India House connected overseas networks with revolutionary and nationalist politics in India.

profiles.name: Madam Bhikaji Cama
profiles.bio: An Indian political activist who campaigned against colonial rule from Europe.
profiles.role: She spoke at international gatherings, supported revolutionary publications and unfurled an early Indian flag design at Stuttgart in 1907.
profiles.context: Her work illustrates the role of diaspora activism and international advocacy.

profiles.name: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar
profiles.bio: A political activist who participated in early 20th-century revolutionary networks and wrote on the 1857 uprising.
profiles.role: He was associated with India House and Abhinav Bharat; he was convicted in a political case and transported to the Cellular Jail.
profiles.context: His later political career and ideology were distinct from his early revolutionary activity and remain subjects of historical discussion.

profiles.name: Khudiram Bose
profiles.bio: A young Bengali revolutionary involved in the Muzaffarpur bomb attack of 1908.
profiles.role: He and Prafulla Chaki targeted a carriage believed to carry magistrate Kingsford; two British women were killed instead. Bose was executed in August 1908.
profiles.context: His case became widely known, while the unintended deaths are an essential part of the historical record.

profiles.name: Prafulla Chaki
profiles.bio: A Bengali revolutionary who worked with Khudiram Bose in the Muzaffarpur operation.
profiles.role: After the attack on 30 April 1908, he was pursued by police and died by suicide to avoid capture.
profiles.context: The incident demonstrates the risks and human consequences of revolutionary violence.

profiles.name: Rash Behari Bose
profiles.bio: A revolutionary organiser associated with early conspiracies and later overseas efforts to build an Indian independence force.
profiles.role: He was linked to the 1912 Delhi-Lahore conspiracy and later helped organise Indian independence networks in East Asia.
profiles.context: His work connected revolutionary groups inside India with expatriate politics.

profiles.name: Lala Har Dayal
profiles.bio: A scholar and anti-colonial activist who helped organise the Ghadar movement among Indian migrants in North America.
profiles.role: He helped establish the Ghadar Party and its newspaper, which called for an end to colonial rule.
profiles.context: The movement's international networks played a part in wartime revolutionary plans.

profiles.name: Kartar Singh Sarabha
profiles.bio: A young Ghadar activist who returned to India to take part in plans for an anti-colonial uprising during World War I.
profiles.role: He was arrested after the failed 1915 uprising plans and executed in Lahore in November 1915.
profiles.context: His life became an important symbol in Punjabi revolutionary memory.

profiles.name: Udham Singh
profiles.bio: An activist from Punjab who was present in the aftermath of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and later travelled abroad.
profiles.role: He shot Michael O'Dwyer in London in March 1940 and was executed in July 1940. He described his action as linked to the 1919 massacre.
profiles.context: His action and its motives should be read in the context of the massacre and the varied methods used by anti-colonial activists.

profiles.name: Ram Prasad Bismil
profiles.bio: A poet and revolutionary organiser associated with the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA).
profiles.role: He was a leading figure in the Kakori train action of 1925 and was executed in December 1927.
profiles.context: The HRA sought to end colonial rule and later evolved into the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.

profiles.name: Ashfaqulla Khan
profiles.bio: A revolutionary associated with the HRA and the Kakori train action.
profiles.role: He was arrested after the Kakori case and executed in Faizabad jail in December 1927.
profiles.context: His association with Bismil is also remembered as a cross-community friendship within a revolutionary organisation.

profiles.name: Chandrashekhar Azad
profiles.bio: A revolutionary who helped reorganise the Hindustan Republican Association as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.
profiles.role: He supported the Kakori network and later worked with Bhagat Singh and other revolutionaries. He died during a police encounter in Allahabad in 1931.
profiles.context: Azad's clandestine work connected several revolutionary episodes in the 1920s and early 1930s.

profiles.name: Bhagat Singh
profiles.bio: A revolutionary socialist whose writings and actions made him one of the most widely remembered figures of the freedom movement.
profiles.role: He was involved in the Saunders case and the 1929 Assembly bombing with Batukeshwar Dutt. He was executed with Rajguru and Sukhdev in 1931.
profiles.context: His surviving writings discuss revolution, socialism, secularism and political organisation. His ideas were broader than armed action alone.

profiles.name: Shivaram Rajguru
profiles.bio: A member of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association and associate of Bhagat Singh.
profiles.role: He took part in the killing of J. P. Saunders in Lahore in 1928 and was executed in 1931.
profiles.context: Rajguru's work forms part of the HSRA's strategy of revolutionary action and public messaging.

profiles.name: Sukhdev Thapar
profiles.bio: A key organiser in the HSRA's Punjab network.
profiles.role: He was implicated in the Lahore Conspiracy Case and executed with Bhagat Singh and Rajguru in March 1931.
profiles.context: Sukhdev's role included organisational work in addition to the actions for which he was tried.

profiles.name: Batukeshwar Dutt
profiles.bio: A revolutionary associated with the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.
profiles.role: He and Bhagat Singh threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly in April 1929 and surrendered. Dutt was sentenced to transportation for life.
profiles.context: The Assembly action was designed as a public political demonstration and caused no deaths.

profiles.name: Surya Sen
profiles.bio: A schoolteacher and revolutionary organiser widely known as Masterda.
profiles.role: He led the Chittagong Armoury Raid on 18 April 1930 and helped establish an underground network.
profiles.context: Women including Pritilata Waddedar and Kalpana Dutta were part of the broader Chittagong revolutionary movement.

profiles.name: Pritilata Waddedar
profiles.bio: A teacher and revolutionary who took part in the Chittagong movement led by Surya Sen.
profiles.role: She led an attack on the Pahartali European Club in September 1932 and died after taking cyanide to avoid capture.
profiles.context: Her life shows women's participation in revolutionary networks beyond the best-known male leaders.

profiles.name: Kalpana Dutta
profiles.bio: A revolutionary associated with Surya Sen's Chittagong group.
profiles.role: She took part in preparations for the armoury raid and later revolutionary activity, was arrested and sentenced to transportation for life, and was released in 1939.
profiles.context: Her memoir offers a participant's account of the Chittagong movement.

profiles.name: Alluri Sitarama Raju
profiles.bio: A leader of the Manyam or Rampa uprising, rooted in tribal grievances against colonial forest policies.
profiles.role: The revolt began with police-station attacks in August 1922 and continued as guerrilla resistance until Raju's capture and killing in May 1924.
profiles.context: The uprising's support and demands were grounded in local Adivasi communities and their land and forest rights.

profiles.name: Subhas Chandra Bose
profiles.bio: A nationalist leader who sought to end British rule through international alliances and an armed force.
profiles.role: He led the Indian National Army and proclaimed the Provisional Government of Azad Hind in 1943.
profiles.context: Bose's wartime alliances with the Axis powers and the INA's campaigns are essential context for assessing this strand of the struggle. His death circumstances remain debated.

profiles.name: B. R. Ambedkar
profiles.bio: Lawyer, scholar, social reformer and political leader who campaigned against caste oppression and for the rights of the Depressed Classes.
profiles.role: He negotiated the Poona Pact in 1932 and chaired the Constitution's Drafting Committee after independence.
profiles.context: Ambedkar's struggle for social equality and political representation was an essential strand of India's transition; it should not be collapsed into armed revolutionary activity.
